meal.title: Simple Calculator in C
meal.objective: Combine input, arithmetic, and output to build a basic calculator program

voice.script: What if your calculator could talk back? How do you read numbers, compute, and show the result? We’ll combine input, arithmetic, and output in one program. First, we include the standard input output library, which gives us the tools to talk to the user. Inside the main function we declare two integer variables to hold the numbers the user types. Using the input command we ask the user to enter two whole numbers and store them. Then we calculate their sum by adding the two variables, and their product by multiplying them. Finally we display both results with the output command, showing a clear message for each. Here’s the complete program. Running it, you’ll see the sum and product displayed. The diagram shows input flowing into calculations and out to the screen. A calculator is just input, math, then output. Try adding subtraction and division to the program.
